questions.text: Explain why New Zealand exports some types of fruit and imports other types.
questions.expectedAnswer: NZ has a comparative advantage in some fruits (e.g., kiwifruit, apples) due to climate/soil...
questions.markingGuide: Identifies that NZ produces too small to influence world price and explains comparative advantage.

questions.text:
On Graph One, label the:
- trade price (Pt)
- amounts of exports and imports in each country (X and M).
questions.expectedAnswer: Trade price (Pt) between PNZ and PPE on both graphs
questions.markingGuide: New supply curve and level of Pt correct. X and M correctly identified.

questions.text: Explain the impact of the trade in oranges on the quantity purchased and total spending on oranges by New Zealand consumers. Refer to Graph One in your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Trade with Peru lowers the price of oranges in NZ to Pt (below domestic PNZ).
questions.markingGuide: Explains that spending is unchanged with reference to the graph — lower price but higher quantity.

questions.text: Compare and contrast the impact of the CPTPP free trade agreement with Peru on growers of different types of fruit in New Zealand.
questions.expectedAnswer: NZ orange growers are negatively affected
questions.markingGuide: Explains that the current account will improve and contrasts effects on different fruit growers.

questions.text: Explain why the world price in the price taker model is shown as a horizontal line.
questions.expectedAnswer: NZ is a small producer relative to the world market, so it cannot influence the world price
questions.markingGuide: Identifies that NZ is too small to influence the world price.

questions.text:
The 2023 exports are labelled as X on Graph Two.

On Graph Two, show the effect of the improved harvest in 2024 on kiwifruit exports by labelling:
- the new supply curve S2024
- the new level of kiwifruit exports as X1.
questions.expectedAnswer: S2024 shifts right of S2023 due to improved harvest (increased supply).
questions.markingGuide: New supply curve S2024 to right of S2023. X1 correctly labelled showing increased exports.

questions.text: Explain how the improved harvest impacts New Zealand consumers' spending on kiwifruit. Refer to Graph Two in your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: The world price (Pw) is unchanged as NZ is a price taker.
questions.markingGuide: Explains that consumer spending is unchanged because the world price and quantity demanded are the same.

questions.text: Explain the impact of the improved harvest on the current account balance. Refer to Graph Two in your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: The improved harvest increases export volume (X to X1) at the same world price.
questions.markingGuide: Explains that increased exports improve the current account balance with reference to export receipts increasing.

questions.text: Compare and contrast the impact of the improved harvest on kiwifruit growers and on workers who pick kiwifruit. Refer to Graph Two in your answer.
questions.markingGuide: Integrates Graph Two into a detailed explanation. Compares effects on growers (revenue/profit) vs workers (employment/wages).

questions.text:
Apart from the USA and Australia, name one of the top five countries New Zealand:

Exports to: ___
Imports from: ___
questions.expectedAnswer: Exports to: China, South Korea, Japan. Imports from: China, South Korea, Japan.
questions.markingGuide: One correct for each of exports and imports.

questions.text: On Graph Three, show the effect of increased exports to the USA.
questions.expectedAnswer: Demand for NZD (DNZ$) shifts right as US importers need NZD to pay for NZ exports.
questions.markingGuide: Graph Three correct — DNZ$ shifts right, exchange rate increases.

questions.text: Explain how an increase in exports affects the NZ$ exchange rate. Refer to Graph Three in your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Increased exports mean US buyers need more NZD to pay for NZ goods.
questions.markingGuide: Provides a detailed explanation of why demand for NZD increases, leading to appreciation.

questions.text: On Graph Four, show the effect of increased imports from the USA.
questions.expectedAnswer: Supply of NZD (SNZ$) shifts right as NZ importers sell NZD to buy US$ to pay for imports.
questions.markingGuide: Graph Four correct — SNZ$ shifts right, exchange rate decreases.

questions.text: Explain how an increase in imports affects the NZ$ exchange rate. Refer to Graph Four in your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Increased imports mean NZ buyers need more US$, so they sell NZD on the foreign exchange market.
questions.markingGuide: Provides a detailed explanation of why supply of NZD increases, leading to depreciation.

questions.text: Compare and contrast the impact of a depreciation of the NZ$ on New Zealand tourists visiting the USA and on New Zealand businesses importing consumer products from the USA.
questions.expectedAnswer: NZ tourists to the USA are negatively affected
questions.markingGuide: Provides a comprehensive explanation of why both groups are negatively affected. Contrasts the effects and assesses which is the greater impact.
